notes: Stress variant: silent and looped (the benchmark's own form: 60 s, music only, looped on 4 of 5 posts), a loss for the whole race after year 1 (the Owned column turns red under water and the gap tints red), long labels with a grey sub-label, a formula-bar verdict, and the band left free so the frozen start row and the scrolling history rows show. Hook: @investment_timeline's biggest post (H43, 5.1M, 22.6x). GoPro IPO: priced $24 on 25 Jun 2014, first-day close $31.34 on 26 Jun 2014. Year-end closes: 2014 $63.22 (recalled; one press summary rounds it to about $65; it only moves the 2014 row), 2015 $18.01, 2016 $8.71, 2017 $7.57, 2018 $4.24, 2019 $4.34, 2020 $8.28, 2021 $10.31, 2022 $4.98, 2023 $3.47, 2024 $1.09. GoPro pays no dividend, so price-only is the total return. Shares: 400 / 31.34 = 12.763. Year-end value = 12.763 × close: 2014 $806.89 (2.02× the IPO close), 2015 $229.87, 2016 $111.17, 2017 $96.62, 2018 $54.12, 2019 $55.39, 2020 $105.68, 2021 $131.59, 2022 $63.56, 2023 $44.29, 2024 $13.91 ≈ $14. 2015 move: 18.01 / 63.22 − 1 = −71.5% ≈ −72%. Total: 13.91 / 400 − 1 = −96.5% ≈ −97%. Formula-bar shortcuts use 12.76 shares: 12.76 × 63.22 = 806.69 ≈ $807; 12.76 × 10.31 = 131.56 ≈ $132; 12.76 × 1.09 = 13.91 ≈ $14. The $400 is the header's round camera price (a HERO3+ Black listed at $399.99 in mid-2014); the spend line is one purchase, flat.
